lines: A fletcher joke should fly straight. Mine <wavy>wobble</wavy> honestly.
Arrows jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with feather on them.
I keep a spare joke near the fletching table. It is not always ready for public use.
I told a joke at the fletching table once. The workstation took it better than the villagers did.
People say I work too much. I say the work is the only one here that listens.
If confidence could be traded, this village would be rich and still somehow underprepared.
I tried taking a day off. The village immediately treated it like an emergency drill.
A good joke needs timing. Around here, timing usually trips over a chicken.
I would laugh louder, but someone would ask me to explain it and ruin everything.
The bell has one joke. It screams, and everyone suddenly remembers they have legs.
Fletcher jokes need good delivery.
I had an arrow joke, but it flew over too fast.
A bow joke only works if the tension is right.
My feather joke is light, but it lands poorly in wind.
I told a target joke and missed the point.
A quiver joke holds more than anyone asked for.
I know a string joke, but it is too taut right now.
The best arrow joke goes straight to the point.
I tried a flight joke. It left before the punchline.
My aim joke was close enough for village standards.
A fletching table has heard every point I failed to make.
The bow laughed once. It was just tension leaving.
I asked the target if the joke landed. It said barely.
A feather pun drifts unless you pin it down.
I would tell a sharper joke, but someone would try to trade for it.
